messages.text: Device won’t get past this

I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Sarah passed this over to me.

It looks like the photo or screenshot did not come through on my side, so I can't see what the device is stuck on. Two quick things:

1. Which model is it (for example NerdQaxe++, Harlo B30, Hammer BC04, Nexus S1)?
2. Can you resend the photo of the screen, or just type out exactly what it says?

Once I see the screen I can tell you what it's waiting on.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Thanks, that photo is clear. The unit itself is healthy: I2C, fan (1358 to 1650 RPM), TMP75 at 26.6 C, TPS546 rail at 1.79 V and the ASIC scan all pass with 2/2 chips found. The only failing line is 5. W5500 ETH: FAIL (No IP obtained), so the board is just not getting an address from your network. Firmware shown is THOR P2 1.0.1 20260818.

First check, one thing only:

1. Is an Ethernet cable plugged from the Thor P2 straight into your router or switch (not a PC, not a powerline adapter)?
2. Look at the two little LEDs on the Ethernet jack on the board. Tell me if either is lit or blinking.

That tells me whether it's a dead link (cable or port) or DHCP on the router side.
It gets access to my router

Good, so the cable and port are alive.

Next check, in your router's admin page open the list of connected devices / DHCP clients and look for the Thor P2. Its W5500 chip uses a WIZnet MAC, which normally starts 00:08:DC.

Tell me which of these you see:

1. An entry for it with an IP address assigned, or
2. No entry at all for that device.

If it does have an IP there, the next thing I'd check is whether your router's DHCP pool is full or has MAC filtering on, since the board is clearly asking and not getting an answer back.
No entry
One line first: let me check whether there's a newer Thor P2 firmware, then the next test.
Searched the web · Thor P2 miner W5500 ETH FAIL no IP obtained firmware
Read harlolabs.com

I couldn't find anything Thor P2 specific on that line beyond what the screen says, so I'm going with the plain reading: the board is sending DHCP requests and nothing is coming back, and your router shows no entry at all for it.

Next check, swap the physical path:

1. Use a different Ethernet cable (a known good one from a PC or console if you have it).
2. Plug it into a different LAN port on the router, not the same one.
3. Pull the power on the Thor P2 for 10 seconds, plug back in, let the self test run.

Then tell me what line 5 says. If it still fails on a second cable and a second port, that points at the W5500 side and not your network, and I'll take it further.
Fail
Used the heliumdeploy-ops-knowledge skill

Thanks, that rules out your cable and your router port. Two cables, two ports, no DHCP entry.

One decisive check before I call it, and it's quick. The board is ESP32 based, so it should have a Wi-Fi side independent of the W5500 Ethernet chip:

1. On your phone, open the Wi-Fi list next to the miner.
2. Tell me if you see an access point from the unit (something like THOR, Bitaxe or NerdQ with characters after it).

Also tell me one thing about the screen: after it prints TEST RESULT: FAIL, does it sit on that screen forever, or does it reboot and run the self test again in a loop?

If Wi-Fi comes up fine and only Ethernet fails, that isolates the fault to the W5500 and I pass my findings to the team.
Nothing in WiFi and sits on this
Handed to the team · W5500 Ethernet fails on two cables and two router ports with no DHCP entry at th

That settles what I can test from here: two cables, two router ports, no DHCP lease at the router, no Wi-Fi AP from the board, and it halts on the self test instead of booting into the miner. Everything else on that screen passes, including the power rail and both ASIC chips, so this is the network side only.

Next rung is a firmware reflash over USB-C, and I want JD (our hardware lead) to hand you the correct Thor P2 image rather than me guessing at it. I've pinged the team and one of them will jump into this chat. Stay in the chat if you can; if you step away you'll get the answer by email.

One thing you can check in the meantime: plug a USB-C data cable from the board into your Mac and tell me whether a new serial device shows up (look under About This Mac, System Report, USB). That tells us the ESP32 is reachable for a reflash.

Faster route if you want it now: our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate (that's JD). He and the community are very active there.
Nothing

Worth ruling out the cable before we read anything into that, since a lot of USB-C cables are charge only.

Two things, in this order:

1. Confirm the cable you used is a data cable (one that has worked for transferring files or flashing something before). If you're not sure, try a second USB-C cable.
2. If you still get nothing, try holding the BOOT button on the board (one of the two small buttons beside the screen) while you plug the USB-C in, then release it after a couple of seconds and check System Report again.

Tell me which button you pressed and what happened. If the ESP32 won't enumerate on a known data cable even in boot mode, that's a board-level finding and JD will take it from there.
Still no IP

Understood, the screen is still failing on line 5. That part I expect, it won't change until the board can either get a lease or be reflashed.

I need the USB answer specifically, because that decides what happens next:

With a known data USB-C cable plugged from the board into the Mac, does anything new appear under System Report, USB? Yes or no is enough.

If no, even after holding the BOOT button while plugging in, then the board can't be reflashed in place and I pass that to JD as a hardware finding.
